controlled_change: Standalone plain_mm_load4 versus unchanged native plain_mm at the same 32-thread group size, with safe Metal arithmetic. No engine changes.
correctness: 80 byte-exact synthetic comparisons over five shapes, eight seeds and two output modes; separate Metal API and shader validation passed.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Lower narrow-projection GPU latency; complete-request benefit must be measured separately.
hypothesis: Loading four input/weight pairs ahead in narrow BF16 projections reduces exposed GPU work before routing without changing accumulation order.
limitations: Synthetic weights and inputs only; no model-level numerical proof.
Operator timings do not measure whole-request speedup.
No precision, model, native selector or default changed.
outcome: Ten alternating operator pairs: median ratio 0.7068 for K10240 N4 T1, 0.6966 for T72, 0.8131 for T128. Tiny K31 N1 regressed to 1.0727. About 5.08MiB peak shared buffers.
smallest_experiment: Replay actual narrow-projection weights and activations before adding a shape-limited runtime candidate and running two normal conversation pairs.
